chunks: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb, from Zurārah ibn Aʿyan, that he said:
By Allah, I have never seen anyone like Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام at all. I asked him and said: “May Allah rectify you; what of birds may be eaten?”

So he said: “Eat whatever flaps, and do not eat whatever glides.” He said: I said, “Eggs in the reed-beds?” He said: “Whatever has its two ends alike, do not eat it; and whatever has its two ends different, then eat it.” I said, “Then water birds?” He said: “Whatever has a crop, eat it; and whatever does not have a crop, do not eat it.”

And in another hadith: “If the bird glides and flaps, and its flapping is more than its gliding, it is eaten; and if its gliding is more than its flapping, it is not eaten. And from the water birds, what has a crop or a spur is eaten, and what does not have a crop or a spur is not eaten.”

key_terms.صَفَّ: glided or soared with wings spread
key_terms.صِيصِيَةٌ: spur or claw-like feature mentioned as an indicator for water birds
key_terms.قَانِصَةٌ: crop or gizzard-like organ used as a legal indicator
key_terms.ٱلطَّيْرِ: birds as the general category under discussion
key_terms.ٱلْبَيْضُ: eggs whose form is used as a sign of permissibility

ai.seo_question: Which birds are halal to eat according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives fiqh criteria for determining which birds and bird eggs are halal to eat. It distinguishes between birds by their manner of flight and physical features, and it also gives indicators for eggs and water birds.
